summary: Teams of 2-4 students create and present a sports media marketing campaign for a rising young athlete, including a written plan and a short promotional teaser video. The campaign must analyze the target audience, competitive landscape, and propose strategies for brand growth, fan engagement, and sponsorships. Teams submit materials before the deadline and deliver a pitch presentation at the competition.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes setup
No more than ten (10) minutes oral presentation
No more than five (5) minutes judges’ questions
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes
submission_requirements: Submit all required items in one combined PDF
PDF must include URL to Video Teaser, Sports Media Marketing Campaign (Title Page, Table of Contents), Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), AI Usage and Documentation Form
Upload completed projects along with the video teaser to a video/file sharing link (Vimeo, YouTube, Dropbox, etc.)
Projects must be viewable on Windows and Mac platforms
Set the access level of your project to one of BPA’s recommended settings
presubmit_items: Sports Media Marketing Campaign, including Title Page, Table of Contents
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: Supporting materials (e.g., research charts, brochures, etc.) for each round of presentations
One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for presentation
Optional: Visuals such as social media mockups, digital advertisements, campaign graphics, etc.
competencies: Develop and justify a sports media marketing strategy that applies to the marketing mix and demonstrates the role of branding and brand loyalty within the global sports industry
Analyze sports audiences and consumer behavior by using demographic, psychographic, and fan engagement data to inform marketing decisions and buying influences
Design integrated marketing communications for sports organizations or events by leveraging digital media, social platforms, and emerging technologies such as influencer marketing
Evaluate ethical, legal, and technological considerations affecting sports media marketing, including sponsorship transparency, data use, and platform selection
Create innovative and creative marketing content that demonstrates originality, strategic thinking, and adaptability to current sports media trends
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to address marketing challenges and optimize campaign outcomes
Demonstrate professional communication and presentation skills by delivering clear, persuasive, and informative pitches using digital and visual media
Collaborate effectively as a team in a marketing environment to plan, produce, and present a cohesive campaign within a global and diverse context

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence & Citation Policy.

The teaser video did not exceed the 30 second limit and the Sports Media Marketing plan did not exceed five (5) pages single-sided. The Title Page, Table of Contents, and Works Cited are not included in the five (5) page limit.

Team submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing a URL to the teaser video, the Sports Media Marketing Plan Campaign, including the Title Page, Table of Contents, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form.

rubric.description: Brand identity is distinctive, cohesive, and strategically positioned
Target audience is precise, research-supported, and clearly informs campaign decisions.
Competitive analysis is thorough, relevant, and used strategically.
Strategy is comprehensive, well-justified, and strongly aligned to the assigned case.
Content strategy is original, integrated, platform-appropriate, and engagement-focused.
Partnership and sponsorship ideas are strategic, realistic, and brand aligned.
Measures are specific, actionable, and support growth and optimization.
Video is original, polished, strategic, and highly effective for engagement.
Campaign is polished, professional, concise, and complete.
Contains very few or no grammar or spelling errors.

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation flows smoothly; team roles, transitions, visuals, supporting materials, and/or teaser video are polished and strategically integrated.
Presentation demonstrates a strong understanding of the campaign, assigned sports context, audience, platforms, partnerships, measurement and teaser’s video role in engagement.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.

judging_notes: Only one (1) team member should complete the submission
The team captain’s contestant ID should be used in any required documents
Contestants will present their Sports Media Marketing Campaign as if pitching to an athlete management team, sports organization, or potential sponsor
Teams may incorporate the campaign teaser video or other visual materials as part of the presentation
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the team within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, teams may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
Finals may be part of the competition
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged team event
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic, or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified
